To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) phenotypic divergence is observed along two abiotic gradients (sulfidicity and darkness) in the livebearing Poecilia mexicanain surface, cave, and sulfidic habitats, 2) genetic divergence is observed along the sulfidic gradient in both surface and cave habitats, 3) genetic divergence is also observed along the light-dark gradient, but only among surface habitats, 4) phenotypic variation along these gradients appears to be heritable,
we found phenotypic, quantitative genetic and population genetic evidence for divergent natural selection in P. mexicana across two environmental gradients.
we found strong genetic and phenotypic divergence among populations along two environmental gradients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolutionary diversification of a fish species along an abiotic gradient.
the evolutionary processes driving phenotypic and molecular divergence in a system with a strong abiotic component, which has not been well studied in the past.
understanding the role of divergent selection in the evolutionary diversification of a species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phenotypic divergence in this system is the result of a complex interaction of genetic divergence, environmental gradients, developmental plasticity and phenotypic selection.
divergent natural selection is driving the phenotypic and population genetic divergence of P. mexicana across the abiotic environmental gradients we investigated.
divergent natural selection drives the evolution of phenotypic diversity and local adaptation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
divergent selection has shaped phenotypic variation and genetic structure in P. mexicana across abiotic gradients.
divergent natural selection drives phenotypic and population genetic divergence in P. mexicana.
the sulfide gradient has been the most influential environmental gradient in the diversification of this species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phenotypic variation and genetic structure are correlated in this system, and that divergent natural selection is driving both.

the same abiotic environmental gradients that are responsible for the phenotypic and molecular differentiation in P. mexicana also create the conditions for the diversification of the entire genus Poecilia.
the phenotypic and molecular diversity observed in P. mexicana is a result of divergent selection along abiotic environmental gradients, including sulfide and darkness.
